findings.evidence: Tips for Success: Test incrementally, Use consistent naming, Leverage GitHub rendering, Export for presentations, Collaborate, Keep updated
findings.fix: The model produces this advice unprompted. Delete the section and add a row for it to docs/audit/recovery/mermaid-diagrams/record.md; keep the Credits section.

findings.evidence: Workflow step 2 Fork is a five-row Read/Change table plus a second type-routing table, not one sequence the agent walks
findings.fix: Keep the navigation pattern. Collapse step 2 to one ordered sequence: read the section 1 type row, then the sections that row requires, then the type file, then step 3.

findings.evidence: Pie: Beyond about seven slices, or for values that are not parts of one whole, use a bar chart in a chart tool instead
findings.fix: Name the Mermaid type: an xyChart bar chart, and point at the xyChart docs already listed in docs/audit/upstream-sources.json, or say the skill does not cover bar charts.

findings.evidence: The Type chosen table repeats the type-file reads already required by the step 2 Fork table
findings.fix: Keep one routing table. Leave the Fork table as the only place that says which type file to open.

findings.evidence: Section 1: Honor an explicitly required diagram format (or ask before substituting)
findings.fix: Make the default one action: when the user names a type, draw that type and add one sentence naming the better type. Ask only when the named type cannot represent the facts.

findings.evidence: Step 4: Only when the user names the host's Mermaid version, validate in a scratch project whose package manager overrides mermaid to that exact version
findings.fix: Give the exact override for one package manager, for example npm: a scratch package.json with overrides.mermaid set to the named version, then the same npx command. Keep the unpinned path as the default.

findings.evidence: Section 4 example draws SG_AUTH --> SG_BILLING, then says that edge is correct only because the user asked for a group-level relationship
findings.fix: Replace the example edge with a case that follows the rule as written: either no cross edge, or the node-to-node edge NODE_AUTH_token --> NODE_BILLING_charge with both direction lines removed. State the group-edge form only as the exception when the user asked for it.

findings.evidence: Social schema draws USER ||..o{ CHAT_GROUP : creates and CHAT_GROUP { uuid created_by FK }, but step 5 says a non-PK FK uses .. and step 2 draws the line from the referenced table
findings.fix: Add the missing relationship USER ||..o{ CHAT_GROUP : "creates through created_by" so the FK column has the line the steps require, or drop created_by from the column list and say the creator is not modeled.

findings.evidence: Worked ERD: TAG }o..o{ ARTICLE : labels uses the conceptual many-to-many while the steps above never show that form
findings.fix: Add one schema-to-diagram step: when there is no junction table, draw one many-to-many line and name it conceptual. Keep the junction-table trap as the other case.
